# HITL FlatSat — System Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| Document | HITL-FLATSAT-SRS |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Verified by | [Test plan](../test/TEST_PLAN.md), [test procedures](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md), test report (`tools/test_report.py`) |

Eight system-level requirements: what the FlatSat must do, each with a measurable pass criterion. The interfaces they rely on are specified in the [ICD](../icd/ICD.md). The thresholds behind the attitude requirements are justified in the [ADCS design note](../design/ADCS_DESIGN.md).

Verification methods: T test, A analysis, I inspection, D demonstration.

## SYS-01

**Autonomous detumble**

From any body rate up to 10 deg/s, the spacecraft shall detect the tumble and reduce its body rate below 2 deg/s within 15 minutes, without ground intervention.

*Rationale.* A satellite leaves its deployer spinning, and a fault can set it spinning again. A pass, and with it the ground, may be hours away; the reaction wheels can only absorb low rates.

*Verification.* Analysis, Test:

- [TC-02](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-02) Firmware unit tests: steps 02.3
- [TC-08](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-08) Attitude control in the loop with 42: steps 08.1, 08.2
- [TC-15](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-15) Comparison with NASA's reference ADCS *(blocked)*: steps 15.1

## SYS-02

**Sun pointing**

In sunlight, the spacecraft shall bring its +X axis within 5 deg of the Sun within 5 minutes of starting sun pointing, and then hold it within 2 deg.

*Rationale.* The solar panels and the power budget depend on facing the Sun.

*Verification.* Analysis, Test:

- [TC-02](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-02) Firmware unit tests: steps 02.3
- [TC-08](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-08) Attitude control in the loop with 42: steps 08.3, 08.4
- [TC-14](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-14) One-orbit endurance: steps 14.1, 14.2, 14.3, 14.4
- [TC-15](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-15) Comparison with NASA's reference ADCS *(blocked)*: steps 15.2

## SYS-03

**Sensor and actuator fault response**

A sensor or actuator that delivers no valid data for 2.5 s shall be declared failed with an event. If the current attitude mode depends on it, the spacecraft shall enter SAFE within 10 s of the failure. Shorter gaps shall not be declared faults, and a device that recovers shall be reported recovered.

*Rationale.* An attitude law running on a dead sensor or actuator can spin the spacecraft up. A fault response that trips on every late reply makes the spacecraft unusable.

*Verification.* Test:

- [TC-07](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-07) Sensor fault persistence and isolation: steps 07.1, 07.2, 07.3, 07.4, 07.5
- [TC-08](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-08) Attitude control in the loop with 42: steps 08.5
- [TC-12](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-12) Actuator, node and bus failures: steps 12.1, 12.2
- [TC-14](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-14) One-orbit endurance: steps 14.5

## SYS-04

**Subsystem node and bus health**

The flight computer shall detect and report the loss of the ADCS or EPS node, including the loss of the CAN bus, within 5 s. In DETUMBLE or SUN_POINT the loss of the ADCS node shall lead to SAFE. A node restart shall be reported with its reset cause, and a node that loses the flight computer shall put its outputs in a safe state.

*Rationale.* The FlatSat is a distributed system; each board must notice when another one stops.

*Verification.* Test:

- [TC-02](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-02) Firmware unit tests: steps 02.1
- [TC-06](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-06) CAN nodes, FlatSat power and the physical wheel: steps 06.1, 06.5, 06.7, 06.8, 06.9
- [TC-12](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-12) Actuator, node and bus failures: steps 12.3, 12.4, 12.5

## SYS-05

**Power management**

Below 25 % simulated battery state of charge the spacecraft shall enter LOW_POWER within 15 s, with the actuators off and the telemetry reduced, and return to SAFE once above 50 % for 10 s. The FlatSat's own supply rails shall be measured to within 2 mA and 10 mV.

*Rationale.* Running the battery flat ends the mission. The real rail measurements are how the FlatSat's power budget is verified.

*Verification.* Test:

- [TC-06](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-06) CAN nodes, FlatSat power and the physical wheel: steps 06.2, 06.4
- [TC-08](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-08) Attitude control in the loop with 42: steps 08.6, 08.7
- [TC-13](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-13) FlatSat power measurement and wheel performance: steps 13.1
- [TC-14](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-14) One-orbit endurance: steps 14.2

## SYS-06

**Commanding and telemetry**

Every telecommand shall be validated (checksum, length, function code, argument ranges) before it runs, and every rejection shall be counted and reported with an event. Housekeeping shall be sent at 1 Hz. Sensor readings shall agree with the simulation's truth within the sensor models' accuracy. The command round trip over the umbilical shall stay below 100 ms.

*Rationale.* A corrupted or out-of-range command must never reach an actuator. Operators and tests depend on timely, truthful telemetry.

*Verification.* Inspection, Test:

- [TC-01](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-01) Interface definitions: steps 01.1, 01.2, 01.3, 01.4
- [TC-02](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-02) Firmware unit tests: steps 02.1
- [TC-04](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-04) Sensor and actuator drivers against 42 truth: steps 04.2, 04.4, 04.5, 04.6, 04.7, 04.8, 04.9, 04.10, 04.11, 04.12, 04.13, 04.14
- [TC-05](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-05) Commanding and telemetry over the umbilical: steps 05.1, 05.2, 05.3, 05.4, 05.5, 05.6, 05.7, 05.8, 05.9, 05.10, 05.11, 05.12
- [TC-08](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-08) Attitude control in the loop with 42: steps 08.8
- [TC-11](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-11) Ground segment end to end (COSMOS): steps 11.1, 11.2, 11.3, 11.4, 11.5, 11.6, 11.7
- [TC-14](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-14) One-orbit endurance: steps 14.5

## SYS-07

**RF link and ground segment**

The spacecraft shall send a beacon every 10 s and hold events and requested data until the next ground contact. Its RF airtime shall stay within 5 % of any hour (10 % including beacons). The ground station shall predict passes to within 15 s and hold telecommands until contact. Corrupted frames shall be rejected and counted.

*Rationale.* A real spacecraft is only reachable during passes, and the 869.4-869.65 MHz band limits airtime to 10 %.

*Verification.* Test, Demonstration:

- [TC-01](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-01) Interface definitions: steps 01.2
- [TC-02](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-02) Firmware unit tests: steps 02.1
- [TC-09](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-09) RF link: steps 09.1, 09.2, 09.3, 09.4, 09.5, 09.6, 09.7, 09.8, 09.9
- [TC-10](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-10) RF pass over NASA Wallops: steps 10.1, 10.2, 10.3, 10.4, 10.5, 10.6
- [TC-11](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-11) Ground segment end to end (COSMOS): steps 11.9, 11.10, 11.11

## SYS-08

**Physical reaction wheel**

The ADCS node shall bring the physical reaction wheel within 20 rpm of a commanded speed within 2 s of a step of up to 300 rpm. In the attitude modes it shall mirror simulated wheel 0 at 1:10. It shall remove motor drive within 1.5 s of losing its commands or its motor power.

*Rationale.* The physical wheel is the FlatSat's hardware twin of the simulated actuator; its tracking is what the hardware campaign measures.

*Verification.* Analysis, Test:

- [TC-02](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-02) Firmware unit tests: steps 02.2
- [TC-06](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-06) CAN nodes, FlatSat power and the physical wheel: steps 06.3, 06.5, 06.6, 06.10
- [TC-12](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-12) Actuator, node and bus failures: steps 12.5
- [TC-13](../test/TEST_PROCEDURES.md#tc-13) FlatSat power measurement and wheel performance: steps 13.2, 13.3, 13.4
